From: Emily Roberts <emily.roberts@novacare.com>

Subject: Renewal planning — residency + APAC standby questions

Hi Olga,

As we approach our renewal (Oct 1), we want to confirm options for two items that are now gating our decision:

1) EU data residency — regulatory team says all PHI-adjacent logs must remain in the EU. We need confirmation of a hardened EU deployment (control plane + inference in eu-west-1) and whether Redwood can guarantee log partitioning for telemetry/trace data.

2) APAC standby — we plan to pilot APAC traffic for our APAC customers later this year. We need an architecture for cross-region failover and a burst capacity option (cold standby that can be ramped to warm). Cost sensitivity is high; we want clear delta pricing for burst capacity and any changes to SLA when failing over.

Can you send a short architecture + price delta and highlight any contract amendments (terms, DPA, residency clause) we should expect? If possible, please include a proposed schedule for a phased rollout (canary -> pilot -> full).

Thanks — Emily
Emily Roberts
Dir., Cloud Ops | NovaCare Health
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear summary. High level answers below; attaching a short pricing appendix and a draft SOW for the rollout.

EU data residency:
- We can provision a dedicated EU tenant (control plane in eu-west, inference nodes in eu-west-1) and offer log partitioning. Operational separation (role-based controls + KMS keys scoped to EU) is included in the Dedicated+Residency addon.
- Contract side: we typically add a residency addendum and an updated DPA that restricts telemetry egress. Ive attached the annotated DPA for your legal team.

APAC standby / cross-region failover:
- We recommend a cold-standby APAC pool (reserved capacity, lower baseline cost) with an automated failover policy. For pilot traffic, we suggest a canary gateway in ap-southeast-1 with prefix caching and limited KV-sync to reduce warm-up latency.
- Pricing: attached PDF includes the incremental monthly delta for cold-standby and two warm-up profiles (30m fast-warm, 6h gradual-warm). Example: cold-standby = $Xk/mo, 30m warm = +Y% on top of committed capacity. Exact numbers in the attachment.

Rollout schedule suggestion (high level):
- Week 0–2: Contract amendments and DPA sign-off
- Week 3–6: EU tenant build + security review (SOC2 evidence handoff)
- Week 7–10: APAC canary deploy + soak testing (traffic shadowing)
- Week 11–14: Pilot (limited region traffic) -> handover

Next steps: if youd like, Ben can run a cost model tuned to your QPS / median sequence length and Monica can draft a mutual action plan for onboarding.

Attachments: redwood-eu-residency-pricing-v2.pdf; sow-eu-apac-failover-draft.docx; dpa-data-processing-addendum-annotated.pdf

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts

- Ben

Thanks Ben — quick notes from legal: 

1) Residency addendum: we can accept EU-only retention for logs and backups but need to preserve metadata required for support (anonymized traces only). We propose a tight clause that references the EU tenant and KMS boundary; well add an audit window (30 days notice) for customer-requested key escrow verification.

2) Failover SLA: we cannot commit to identical uptime during cross-region failover unless customer purchases the warm-warm profile (which incurs higher baseline). Well offer an SLA credit schedule that scales by failover profile: cold-standby = reduced SLA during ramp (credit table attached in SOW).

3) DPA redlines: I annotated the DPA; most redlines are acceptable but well flag the backup custody language to discuss with NovaCare.

Markus Klein

Paul/Emily — quick answers and next steps: 

• 30m fast-warm RTO & latency: in our tests the P99 tail latency stabilizes within 20–35 minutes depending on model KV size; we guarantee a warm-up SLA metric tied to choice of warm profile (details in SOW appendix). During the first 30 minutes we recommend a traffic shaping policy (ramp to 25% -> 60% -> 100%) to avoid tail amplification.

• KV cache strategy: for canary we do region-specific caches with prefix-sync for critical keys (small set) and shadowing for non-critical traffic. That keeps shadow costs minimal and avoids full double-billing for every inference. We'll include exact cache sync behavior in the technical runbook attachment.

Action items:
- Ben to produce a refined cost delta table (tomorrow EOD).
- Monica to draft a Mutual Action Plan and onboarding milestones (due Friday).
- Markus to produce the final annotated DPA + suggested residency addendum text (EOD Friday).
- Olga to submit a revised SOW with SLA credit table and warm profiles (EOD Friday).

If that timeline works we can aim to have contract ready for signature by Sep 2 and technical kickoff the week of Sep 6.

Best,
Olga
